task.title: Validate every pull request
task.shortdesc: Run opend validate in GitHub Actions so problems show inline on the pull request, before anything is merged or published.

context.p: The starter template ships .github/workflows/validate.yml, which runs the published CLI with npx @opend/cli@0. Until the CLI is published to npm, build it from a checkout of the OpenD repository instead, as this workflow does.

step.cmd: Add a workflow to the docs repository.

stepxmp.codeblock: name: Validate docs on: pull_request: push: branches: [main, 'v*'] jobs: validate: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: path: docs - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: repository: desktopmachineshop/opend path: opend - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4 with: package_json_file: opend/package.json - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 22 - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build working-directory: opend - run: node opend/packages/cli/dist/bin.js validate docs --format github

step.cmd: Optional: add --strict to fail on warnings too.

info.p: This site's own CI validates site/ with --strict.

result.p: With --format github, each problem becomes a workflow annotation on the line it is about, titled with its code.
On the hosted platform the worker runs the same validation on every push, and a failing push never goes live. CI tells authors earlier.
